title: Managing Warehouse Robots Like a Computer Network
hints: LoRR 2026 problem
Warehouse-like map: plan robot moves to finish as many orders as possible
Approach: borrow ideas from computer networks
en: Good afternoon, everyone. Our project works on the **League of Robot Runners 2026** problem, or **LoRR** for short. We study **a warehouse-like map**: how to plan the robots' moves so that they **finish as many orders as possible**. Our approach borrows ideas from **computer networks**.
zh: 大家下午好。我们的项目做的是 **2026 年机器人跑者联赛（LoRR）** 的问题。我们研究的是：在一张**类似仓库的地图**上，怎么安排机器人走路，让它们**完成尽可能多的派单任务**。我们的做法是借用**计算机网络**的思路。

segs.en: Good afternoon, everyone. Our project works on the **League of Robot Runners 2026** problem, or **LoRR** for short.
segs.zh: 大家下午好。我们的项目做的是 **2026 年机器人跑者联赛（LoRR）** 的问题。

segs.en: We study **a warehouse-like map**: how to plan the robots' moves so that they **finish as many orders as possible**.
segs.zh: 我们研究的是：在一张**类似仓库的地图**上，怎么安排机器人走路，让它们**完成尽可能多的派单任务**。

segs.en: Our approach borrows ideas from **computer networks**.
segs.zh: 我们的做法是借用**计算机网络**的思路。

title: The task: hundreds of robots, narrow doors
hints: Score = orders finished in 5,000 ticks
3 decisions: assign / route / execute
16 rooms, 31 doors, 1 cell wide, 200–300 robots
Blue path: 8 doors
en: 【指左图】 Each grey dot is a robot. Robots pick up and deliver orders for **5,000 ticks**. A tick is one time step. The score is **how many orders they finish**. 【指右边 1、2、3】 Each tick, the program decides three things: **who takes which order, which way to go, and whether to move now**. 【指下方数字】 We use the official room map: **16 rooms, 31 doors**, most doors **one cell wide**, and **200 to 300 robots**. 【指蓝色路线】 This one order passes **eight doors**.
zh: 【指左图】每个灰点是一台机器人。车在 **5000 拍**里不停取货送货，一拍就是一个时间步。比的是**完成多少单**。【指右边 1、2、3】程序每一拍决定三件事：**谁接哪单、走哪条路、现在走不走**。【指下方数字】我们用官方房间图：**16 个房间、31 道门**，大多数门只有**一格宽**，车有 **200 到 300 台**。【指蓝色路线】这一单就要穿过 **8 道门**。

segs.en: 【指左图】 Each grey dot is a robot. Robots pick up and deliver orders for **5,000 ticks**. A tick is one time step. The score is **how many orders they finish**.
segs.zh: 【指左图】每个灰点是一台机器人。车在 **5000 拍**里不停取货送货，一拍就是一个时间步。比的是**完成多少单**。

segs.en: 【指右边 1、2、3】 Each tick, the program decides three things: **who takes which order, which way to go, and whether to move now**.
segs.zh: 【指右边 1、2、3】程序每一拍决定三件事：**谁接哪单、走哪条路、现在走不走**。

segs.en: 【指下方数字】 We use the official room map: **16 rooms, 31 doors**, most doors **one cell wide**, and **200 to 300 robots**.
segs.zh: 【指下方数字】我们用官方房间图：**16 个房间、31 道门**，大多数门只有**一格宽**，车有 **200 到 300 台**。

segs.en: 【指蓝色路线】 This one order passes **eight doors**.
segs.zh: 【指蓝色路线】这一单就要穿过 **8 道门**。

title: The longer it runs, the slower it gets
hints: Ran starter + 2024 champion
Every curve falls
No errors, no collisions
Something builds up over time
Hand over to Speaker 2
en: We started by running two existing programs: the official starter program and the 2024 champion's way of giving out orders. 【指三组曲线】 We saw something strange: **the longer it runs, the slower it gets.** 【指左边 127 和 37】 With the champion's method, averaged over 60 runs, orders finished per 500 ticks fell from **127 to 37**. There were **no errors and no collisions**. So something was **building up over time**. Speaker 2 will show what.
zh: 我们先跑了两个现有程序：官方起始程序，和 2024 届冠军的派单方法。【指三组曲线】我们看到一个奇怪的现象：**跑得越久，越慢。**【指左边 127 和 37】用冠军的派单，60 局平均，每 500 拍完成的单数从 **127 降到 37**。而且**没有报错、没有碰撞**。所以是有什么东西在**随时间累积**。下面讲者 2 来讲是什么。

segs.en: We started by running two existing programs: the official starter program and the 2024 champion's way of giving out orders.
segs.zh: 我们先跑了两个现有程序：官方起始程序，和 2024 届冠军的派单方法。

segs.en: 【指三组曲线】 We saw something strange: **the longer it runs, the slower it gets.**
segs.zh: 【指三组曲线】我们看到一个奇怪的现象：**跑得越久，越慢。**

segs.en: 【指左边 127 和 37】 With the champion's method, averaged over 60 runs, orders finished per 500 ticks fell from **127 to 37**.
segs.zh: 【指左边 127 和 37】用冠军的派单，60 局平均，每 500 拍完成的单数从 **127 降到 37**。

segs.en: There were **no errors and no collisions**. So something was **building up over time**. Speaker 2 will show what.
segs.zh: 而且**没有报错、没有碰撞**。所以是有什么东西在**随时间累积**。下面讲者 2 来讲是什么。

title: Robots jam at one narrow door
figs: 图 3 第 3000 拍堵门截图
hints: Tick 3,000: 97 robots still have to cross door 6 inward (incl. not yet at the door)
Easy orders first → 38% → 86% must cross
Face to face in a 1-cell door
3.4–7.0 vs 26 per 500 ticks
More robots, fewer crossings
en: Thank you. We watched the replay tick by tick. 【指左图黑圈】 At tick 3,000, **97 robots** still have to go through **door 6** into the lower-left rooms. Some are waiting at the door; the rest are on the way. 【指右边第二张卡】 Why? Easy orders are done first, so more and more of the orders left need this door: from **38 percent up to 86 percent**. 【指第三张卡】 Robots then meet **face to face** in the one-cell door. Later in the run, only **3.4 to 7** robots get through per 500 ticks. When they take turns properly, **26** get through. **More robots, fewer crossings.**
zh: 谢谢。我们一拍一拍地看回放。【指左图黑圈】第 3000 拍，还要穿过**门 6** 进左下房间的车有 **97 台**：有的已经堵在门口，有的还在路上。【指右边第二张卡】为什么？好做的单先做完，剩下的单里要过这道门的越来越多：从 **38% 涨到最多 86%**。【指第三张卡】于是车在一格宽的门口**面对面顶住**。后半程每 500 拍只过 **3.4 到 7 台**；如果轮流有序，能过 **26 台**。**车越多，过得越少。**

segs.en: Thank you. We watched the replay tick by tick.
segs.zh: 谢谢。我们一拍一拍地看回放。

segs.en: 【指左图黑圈】 At tick 3,000, **97 robots** still have to go through **door 6** into the lower-left rooms. Some are waiting at the door; the rest are on the way.
segs.zh: 【指左图黑圈】第 3000 拍，还要穿过**门 6** 进左下房间的车有 **97 台**：有的已经堵在门口，有的还在路上。

segs.en: 【指右边第二张卡】 Why? Easy orders are done first, so more and more of the orders left need this door: from **38 percent up to 86 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指右边第二张卡】为什么？好做的单先做完，剩下的单里要过这道门的越来越多：从 **38% 涨到最多 86%**。

segs.en: 【指第三张卡】 Robots then meet **face to face** in the one-cell door. Later in the run, only **3.4 to 7** robots get through per 500 ticks. When they take turns properly, **26** get through. **More robots, fewer crossings.**
segs.zh: 【指第三张卡】于是车在一格宽的门口**面对面顶住**。后半程每 500 拍只过 **3.4 到 7 台**；如果轮流有序，能过 **26 台**。**车越多，过得越少。**

title: Prior work: four groups of methods
hints: 4 groups: assignment / route guidance / planners (PIBT) / jam handling
Each improves its own step
None looks at the whole system with many factors together
en: 【依次指四张卡】 Prior methods fall into four groups. **Order assignment** picks close, cheap orders. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread to other roads. **Planners like PIBT** decide who moves first and avoid collisions. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle, or handles robots at narrow passages. 【指底部黄框】 In the methods we read, each one improves **its own step**. None looks at **the whole system** and weighs **many factors together**.
zh: 【依次指四张卡】前人的方法分四类。**派单**挑近的、便宜的单；**选路**给拥挤的路加代价，让车分散到别的路；**PIBT 这类规划**决定谁先走、避免碰撞；**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着，或者处理窄道上的车。【指底部黄框】在我们读到的方法里，每一种只优化**自己那一步**，没有一种从**整体**出发、**同时考虑多个因素**来解决这个问题。

segs.en: 【依次指四张卡】 Prior methods fall into four groups.
segs.zh: 【依次指四张卡】前人的方法分四类。

segs.en: **Order assignment** picks close, cheap orders. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread to other roads. **Planners like PIBT** decide who moves first and avoid collisions. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle, or handles robots at narrow passages.
segs.zh: **派单**挑近的、便宜的单；**选路**给拥挤的路加代价，让车分散到别的路；**PIBT 这类规划**决定谁先走、避免碰撞；**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着，或者处理窄道上的车。

segs.en: 【指底部黄框】 In the methods we read, each one improves **its own step**. None looks at **the whole system** and weighs **many factors together**.
segs.zh: 【指底部黄框】在我们读到的方法里，每一种只优化**自己那一步**，没有一种从**整体**出发、**同时考虑多个因素**来解决这个问题。

title: Our idea: treat the warehouse as a computer network
hints: Want a more systematic approach
Teammate: implemented + optimized backbone traffic scheduling at a global carrier → network angle
Door = link; order = packet through routers; more robots, fewer crossings = congestion
Why networks: whole-system view; proven routing + scheduling; hands-on experience
Hypothesis: borrow routing + scheduling → test
Hand over to Speaker 3 (technical part)
en: So we wanted a **more systematic** way to solve the problem. One of us has **implemented and optimized traffic scheduling algorithms on a global carrier's backbone network**, so we decided to explore from the **computer network** angle. 【指左边三行】 Seen this way, **a door is like a link**, **an order is like a packet** passing a chain of routers, and **more robots but fewer crossings is like network congestion**. 【指右边 1、2、3】 Networks fit for three reasons. They look at **the whole system**: for decades they have handled **many senders sharing few links**. They have proven methods for **routing**, which path to take, and **scheduling**, who goes when. And we have **hands-on experience** with these methods, so we know what they assume. 【指底部深色框】 Our guess: **borrowing routing and scheduling from networks may help robots finish more orders.** We had to test it. Speaker 3 will explain the model.
zh: 所以我们想用**更系统**的思路和方法来解决这个问题。我们组有同学**在全球网络运营商的骨干网上实施和优化过流量调度算法**，所以我们决定从**计算机网络**的角度去探索。【指左边三行】从这个角度看，**门像一条链路**，**一单像经过一串路由器的数据包**，**车越多、过得越少，就像网络拥塞**。【指右边 1、2、3】网络合适有三个原因：它看的是**整个系统**，几十年来解决的就是**很多发送者共用少数线路**；它有成熟的**路由**（走哪条路）和**调度**（谁什么时候走）方法；我们对这些方法有**实际经验**，知道它们的前提。【指底部深色框】我们的猜想：**借用网络的路由和调度，也许能让车完成更多的单。** 这要靠实验检验。下面讲者 3 讲模型。

segs.en: So we wanted a **more systematic** way to solve the problem. One of us has **implemented and optimized traffic scheduling algorithms on a global carrier's backbone network**, so we decided to explore from the **computer network** angle.
segs.zh: 所以我们想用**更系统**的思路和方法来解决这个问题。我们组有同学**在全球网络运营商的骨干网上实施和优化过流量调度算法**，所以我们决定从**计算机网络**的角度去探索。

segs.en: 【指左边三行】 Seen this way, **a door is like a link**, **an order is like a packet** passing a chain of routers, and **more robots but fewer crossings is like network congestion**.
segs.zh: 【指左边三行】从这个角度看，**门像一条链路**，**一单像经过一串路由器的数据包**，**车越多、过得越少，就像网络拥塞**。

segs.en: 【指右边 1、2、3】 Networks fit for three reasons. They look at **the whole system**: for decades they have handled **many senders sharing few links**. They have proven methods for **routing**, which path to take, and **scheduling**, who goes when. And we have **hands-on experience** with these methods, so we know what they assume.
segs.zh: 【指右边 1、2、3】网络合适有三个原因：它看的是**整个系统**，几十年来解决的就是**很多发送者共用少数线路**；它有成熟的**路由**（走哪条路）和**调度**（谁什么时候走）方法；我们对这些方法有**实际经验**，知道它们的前提。

segs.en: 【指底部深色框】 Our guess: **borrowing routing and scheduling from networks may help robots finish more orders.** We had to test it.
segs.zh: 【指底部深色框】我们的猜想：**借用网络的路由和调度，也许能让车完成更多的单。** 这要靠实验检验。

segs.en: Speaker 3 will explain the model.
segs.zh: 下面讲者 3 讲模型。

title: The model: 16 rooms, 31 links, routers at the doors
hints: 3,646 cells → 16 nodes, 31 links
Door 6 is a cut
Sender / packet / half-duplex link / router port
Router at the door: 4.2×; 30% of waiting on 10% of area
en: Thank you. First, the model. 【指左图】 We turned the map into a network: **16 rooms are nodes, 31 doors are links**. 【指红线门 6】 **Door 6 is a cut**: remove it, and the four lower-left rooms are cut off. 【指右边四行】 Giving out orders is the **sender**. A **robot is a packet**. A **door is a half-duplex link**: one direction at a time. And the area near a door works as the **router**, deciding who goes next. 【指黄色框】 Why at the door? Near a door, robots stand still **4.2 times** as long as they move. The door area is **10 percent of the map but holds 30 percent of all waiting**.
zh: 谢谢。先讲模型。【指左图】我们把地图变成一张网络：**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**。【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：拿掉它，左下 4 个房间就和其他房间断开了。【指右边四行】派单是**发送端**，**机器人是数据包**，**门是半双工链路**：一次只走一个方向。门口附近就是**路由器**，决定谁先走。【指黄色框】为什么在门口？门附近，车停着的时间是走的 **4.2 倍**；门口这一圈**只占 10% 的面积，却占了 30% 的等待**。

segs.en: Thank you. First, the model. 【指左图】 We turned the map into a network: **16 rooms are nodes, 31 doors are links**.
segs.zh: 谢谢。先讲模型。【指左图】我们把地图变成一张网络：**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**。

segs.en: 【指红线门 6】 **Door 6 is a cut**: remove it, and the four lower-left rooms are cut off.
segs.zh: 【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：拿掉它，左下 4 个房间就和其他房间断开了。

segs.en: 【指右边四行】 Giving out orders is the **sender**. A **robot is a packet**. A **door is a half-duplex link**: one direction at a time. And the area near a door works as the **router**, deciding who goes next.
segs.zh: 【指右边四行】派单是**发送端**，**机器人是数据包**，**门是半双工链路**：一次只走一个方向。门口附近就是**路由器**，决定谁先走。

segs.en: 【指黄色框】 Why at the door? Near a door, robots stand still **4.2 times** as long as they move. The door area is **10 percent of the map but holds 30 percent of all waiting**.
segs.zh: 【指黄色框】为什么在门口？门附近，车停着的时间是走的 **4.2 倍**；门口这一圈**只占 10% 的面积，却占了 30% 的等待**。

title: Similar, but not the same
figs: 图 5 仓库与网络的对应
hints: 1 cannot be dropped
2 waiting robot blocks a cell
3 fixed fleet
4 no retransmission (1986 vs face to face)
Closer to a lossless data-center network
en: But similar is not the same. 【指右边四张卡】 There are four differences. **One: robots cannot be dropped**; a router can drop a packet, a robot can only wait. **Two: a waiting robot blocks a cell.** **Three: the number of robots is fixed.** **Four: the cause is different.** The 1986 internet collapse came from **resending data**. Robots do not resend; they just meet face to face. 【指底部一行】 So we skip methods made for resending. Robots are closer to a **lossless network**, one that never drops data.
zh: 但像不等于一样。【指右边四张卡】有四点不同。**第一，车不能丢**：路由器可以丢包，车只能等。**第二，等着的车占着格子。** **第三，车数固定。****第四，堵的原因不同。** 1986 年互联网崩溃来自**数据重发**；车不会重发，只是面对面顶住。【指底部一行】所以对付重发的办法不借。车更接近**无损网络**，也就是从不丢数据的网络。

segs.en: But similar is not the same. 【指右边四张卡】 There are four differences.
segs.zh: 但像不等于一样。【指右边四张卡】有四点不同。

segs.en: **One: robots cannot be dropped**; a router can drop a packet, a robot can only wait. **Two: a waiting robot blocks a cell.** **Three: the number of robots is fixed.**
segs.zh: **第一，车不能丢**：路由器可以丢包，车只能等。**第二，等着的车占着格子。** **第三，车数固定。**

segs.en: **Four: the cause is different.** The 1986 internet collapse came from **resending data**. Robots do not resend; they just meet face to face.
segs.zh: **第四，堵的原因不同。** 1986 年互联网崩溃来自**数据重发**；车不会重发，只是面对面顶住。

segs.en: 【指底部一行】 So we skip methods made for resending. Robots are closer to a **lossless network**, one that never drops data.
segs.zh: 【指底部一行】所以对付重发的办法不借。车更接近**无损网络**，也就是从不丢数据的网络。

title: Routing or scheduling? The ceiling decides
hints: Routing first: did not help
11 rerouting methods all worse
Scheduling → next slides
en: Which to borrow: routing or scheduling? We tried **routing first**. It did not help. Here is why. 【指 1】 The lower-left rooms hold **906 of 3,614** room cells: **25 percent**. 【指 2】 If an order's two ends are on different sides, it needs door 6: **2 times 0.25 times 0.75 is 37.6 percent**. The real task file gives 38.5. 【指 3 和公式】 Door 6 passes **26 robots per 500 ticks**, so the map finishes at most **26 divided by 0.376, which is 69 orders**. A new route cannot raise this. 【指底部 11】 Indeed, **all 11 rerouting methods we tried were worse**. The real question is **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**. That is scheduling.
zh: 借路由还是借调度？我们**先试了路由**，没用。原因如下。【指 1】左下房间占 3614 个房间格里的 **906 个**：906 ÷ 3614 = **25%**。【指 2】一单两头在门的两侧，就要过门 6：**2 × 0.25 × 0.75 = 37.6%**，真实任务文件里是 38.5%。【指 3 和公式】门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，所以整张图最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 = 69 单**。换路提高不了它。【指底部 11】我们后来试的 **11 种换路办法确实全部变差**。真正的问题是**派多少车、哪边先走**，这是调度。

segs.en: Which to borrow: routing or scheduling? We tried **routing first**. It did not help. Here is why.
segs.zh: 借路由还是借调度？我们**先试了路由**，没用。原因如下。

segs.en: 【指 1】 The lower-left rooms hold **906 of 3,614** room cells: **25 percent**.
【指 2】 If an order's two ends are on different sides, it needs door 6: **2 times 0.25 times 0.75 is 37.6 percent**. The real task file gives 38.5.
【指 3 和公式】 Door 6 passes **26 robots per 500 ticks**, so the map finishes at most **26 divided by 0.376, which is 69 orders**. A new route cannot raise this.
segs.zh: 【指 3 和公式】门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，所以整张图最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 = 69 单**。换路提高不了它。

segs.en: 【指底部 11】 Indeed, **all 11 rerouting methods we tried were worse**. The real question is **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**. That is scheduling.
segs.zh: 【指底部 11】我们后来试的 **11 种换路办法确实全部变差**。真正的问题是**派多少车、哪边先走**，这是调度。

title: Scheduling 1: the TCP window principle
figs: TCP / BBR 概念图（示意，不是实测数据）
hints: How many robots should head for door 6 at once?
TCP window: sent but not yet confirmed
Too little in flight: link idle; too much: only a queue
Best: in flight = bandwidth × delay; BBR aims here
Robots are worse: extra robots block the other side → crossings fall
So cap robots heading for the door at bandwidth × delay

segs.en: How many robots should head for door 6 at the same time? Networks answer this question with the **TCP window**: how much data may be **sent but not yet confirmed**.
segs.zh: 同时该有多少车奔向门 6？网络用 **TCP 窗口**回答这个问题：允许多少数据**已经发出、还没确认**。

segs.en: 【指左图上半】 This is the classic picture. With too little data in flight, the link **sometimes sits idle**. With too much, the link **cannot go faster**: the extra data just waits in a queue, 【指左图下半】 and delay goes up.
segs.zh: 【指左图上半】这是经典的图：在途数据太少，链路**有时空着**；太多，链路**也不会更快**，多出来的数据只是排队，【指左图下半】时延越来越长。

segs.en: 【指橙色虚线】 The best point is where data in flight equals **bandwidth times delay**. Google's **BBR** aims right at this point; the next slide shows how.
segs.zh: 【指橙色虚线】最好的点是在途数据等于**带宽 × 时延**。谷歌的 **BBR** 就直接瞄准这个点，下一页讲它怎么做到。

segs.en: 【指右边最后两条】 For robots it is **worse than a queue**. Extra robots stand in the door area and **block the other side**, so crossings do not stay flat, they **fall**. So we cap the robots heading for the door at **bandwidth times delay**.
segs.zh: 【指右边最后两条】机器人比排队**更糟**：多出来的车站在门口区，**挡住对面**，过门数不是持平，而是**下降**。所以我们把奔向门的车限制在**带宽 × 时延**。

With too little data in flight, the link **sometimes sits idle**. With too much, the link **cannot go faster**: the extra data just waits in a queue, 【指左图下半】 and delay goes up. 【指橙色虚线】 The best point is where data in flight equals **bandwidth times delay**. Google's **BBR** aims right at this point; the next slide shows how. 【指右边最后两条】 For robots it is **worse than a queue**. Extra robots stand in the door area and **block the other side**, so crossings do not stay flat, they **fall**. So we cap the robots heading for the door at **bandwidth times delay**.

title: Scheduling 1: why BBR, not ordinary TCP
figs: BBR 与丢包型 TCP 概念图（示意，不是实测数据）
hints: Reno / CUBIC: grow until a packet is lost
Robots never dropped → no stop signal → 211 in flight
BBR: max delivery rate × min round-trip time, no loss needed
Use the MIN delay: a jam makes delay longer → would raise the window
Our quota: measured bandwidth × travel time
Rounds 50–51: BBR-style cap on missed narrow spots (delay 2.2–2.9× model): big losses gone, +0.08% → keep fixed quota
Not copied: BBR probing state machine, pacing

segs.en: Why BBR, and not ordinary TCP? Ordinary TCP, like **Reno or CUBIC**, keeps opening its window **until a packet is lost**, then backs off. 【指左图灰线】 A lost packet is its only stop signal.
segs.zh: 为什么是 BBR，而不是普通 TCP？普通 TCP，比如 **Reno、CUBIC**，会一直把窗口开大，**直到丢了一个包**才退回来。【指左图灰线】丢包是它唯一的“停”信号。

segs.en: 【指左图红线】 Robots are **never dropped**, so that signal never comes. The window would just keep growing. That is what we measured: **211** robots heading for one door.
segs.zh: 【指左图红线】机器人**从来不会丢**，所以这个信号永远不来，窗口会一直涨。我们实测到的正是这样：**211 台**车奔向同一道门。

segs.en: 【指左图蓝线】 **BBR** does not wait for a loss. It measures the **highest delivery rate** and the **shortest round-trip time**, and keeps in flight near their product. It needs no loss, so it fits robots.
segs.zh: 【指左图蓝线】**BBR** 不等丢包。它测出**最大送达速率**和**最短往返时间**，让在途量保持在两者乘积附近。它不需要丢包，所以适合机器人。

segs.en: 【指右边第二条】 One detail matters: BBR uses the **shortest** delay, not the current one. A jam makes delay longer. If the window followed the current delay, **the jam would raise the window** and make itself worse.
segs.zh: 【指右边第二条】有一个细节很关键：BBR 用的是**最短**时延，不是当前时延。堵车会让时延变长；如果窗口跟着当前时延走，**堵车反而会把窗口抬高**，越堵越厉害。

segs.en: 【指右边下框】 We used this twice. Our quota comes from **measured** door bandwidth and travel time. Later, on narrow spots our model had missed, the real delay was **2.2 to 2.9 times** the model, so we tried a **BBR-style cap**: highest crossing rate times shortest delay. The big losses went away, but the average gain was only **0.08 percent**, so we kept the simple fixed quota.
segs.zh: 【指右边下框】我们用了两次。名额本身来自**实测的**门带宽和走到门口的时间。后来在模型漏掉的窄处，实际时延是模型的 **2.2 到 2.9 倍**，我们就试了 **BBR 式上限**：最大过门速率 × 最短时延。大的损失没有了，但平均只多 **0.08%**，所以保留简单的固定名额。

The window would just keep growing. That is what we measured: **211** robots heading for one door. 【指左图蓝线】 **BBR** does not wait for a loss. It measures the **highest delivery rate** and the **shortest round-trip time**, and keeps in flight near their product. It needs no loss, so it fits robots. 【指右边第二条】 One detail matters: BBR uses the **shortest** delay, not the current one. A jam makes delay longer. If the window followed the current delay, **the jam would raise the window** and make itself worse. 【指右边下框】 We used this twice. Our quota comes from **measured** door bandwidth and travel time. Later, on narrow spots our model had missed, the real delay was **2.2 to 2.9 times** the model, so we tried a **BBR-style cap**: highest crossing rate times shortest delay. The big losses went away, but the average gain was only **0.08 percent**, so we kept the simple fixed quota.

title: Scheduling 1: our per-door quota = bandwidth × delay
figs: 图 9 在途车与过门数
hints: Count: holds a door-6 order, not crossed, even far away
Full → give an order that does not cross
Bandwidth 26 / 500 ticks → 13 per direction
Delay 247 ticks × 2.23 → 15 in; 158 ticks → 10 out
Red: 211 in flight, 3 cross; blue: about 25 (knee), 26 cross
AIMD (self-adjusting) worse than fixed → keep formula

segs.en: Our quota counts robots that **hold a door-6 order but have not crossed yet**, even far away. 【指右边第一条】 When it is full, that robot gets **an order that does not cross**.
segs.zh: 我们的名额数的是**接了过门 6 的单、还没过门**的车，哪怕离门还很远。【指右边第一条】名额满了，就给这台车派**一单不过门的**。

segs.en: 【指公式】 Both numbers are measured. Bandwidth: door 6 passes **26 robots per 500 ticks**, **13 per direction**. Delay: **247 ticks** to reach the door, times **2.23** for breakdowns. **2.23 times 247 divided by 500 times 13 is 14.3**, so **15 going in**. Going out takes 158 ticks, so **10**.
【指左图红线】 The test: with no control, **211** robots head for the door and only **3** get through. 【指蓝点】 With the quota, about **25** head for it, right at the knee, and **26** get through.
segs.zh: 【指左图红线】实验结果：不管门时，**211 台**车奔向门，只过 **3 台**。【指蓝点】用名额，25 台左右奔向门，正好在拐点上，过 **26 台**。

segs.en: 【指右边最后一条】 Unlike TCP, nothing is dropped and our quota is **fixed**. A self-adjusting window, **AIMD**, did worse than the fixed value, so we kept the formula.
segs.zh: 【指右边最后一条】和 TCP 不同，这里不丢包，名额也是**固定**的。自己调整的窗口 **AIMD** 比固定值差，所以保留公式。

en: Our quota counts robots that **hold a door-6 order but have not crossed yet**, even far away. 【指右边第一条】 When it is full, that robot gets **an order that does not cross**. 【指公式】 Both numbers are measured. Bandwidth: door 6 passes **26 robots per 500 ticks**, **13 per direction**. Delay: **247 ticks** to reach the door, times **2.23** for breakdowns. **2.23 times 247 divided by 500 times 13 is 14.3**, so **15 going in**. Going out takes 158 ticks, so **10**. 【指左图红线】 The test: with no control, **211** robots head for the door and only **3** get through. 【指蓝点】 With the quota, about **25** head for it, right at the knee, and **26** get through. 【指右边最后一条】 Unlike TCP, nothing is dropped and our quota is **fixed**. A self-adjusting window, **AIMD**, did worse than the fixed value, so we kept the formula.
zh: 我们的名额数的是**接了过门 6 的单、还没过门**的车，哪怕离门还很远。【指右边第一条】名额满了，就给这台车派**一单不过门的**。【指公式】两个数都是实测的。带宽：门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，每个方向 **13 台**。时延：走到门口 **247 拍**，乘故障放慢 **2.23**。**2.23 × 247 ÷ 500 × 13 = 14.3**，所以**进 15 台**；出来要走 158 拍，所以**出 10 台**。【指左图红线】实验结果：不管门时，**211 台**车奔向门，只过 **3 台**。【指蓝点】用名额，25 台左右奔向门，正好在拐点上，过 **26 台**。【指右边最后一条】和 TCP 不同，这里不丢包，名额也是**固定**的。自己调整的窗口 **AIMD** 比固定值差，所以保留公式。

title: Scheduling 2: one direction at a time
hints: 1-cell door = half-duplex link: one direction at a time
Serve one side; other side steps back 4 cells
Side empty → wind down → switch
4-cell step-back: no network counterpart

segs.en: Method two is the **door rule**. A one-cell door is a **half-duplex link**: it carries **one direction at a time**.
segs.zh: 方法二是**门口规则**。一格宽的门就是**半双工链路**：**一次只走一个方向**。

segs.en: 【指上面三格图，从左到右】 The door serves one side. Robots on the other side **step back four cells** to keep the exit clear. When this side is empty, the door winds down, then **switches**.
segs.zh: 【指上面三格图，从左到右】门先服务一边，对面的车**退出门口 4 格**，把出口让出来；这一边走空了，门就收尾，然后**换向**。

segs.en: 【指 4 cells】 The step-back has **no network counterpart**: a waiting packet sits in a buffer, but **a waiting robot blocks the way**.
segs.zh: 【指 4 cells】退让这一条**网络里没有**：等着的数据包待在缓存里，但**等着的车会挡路**。

en: Method two is the **door rule**. A one-cell door is a **half-duplex link**: it carries **one direction at a time**. 【指上面三格图，从左到右】 The door serves one side. Robots on the other side **step back four cells** to keep the exit clear. When this side is empty, the door winds down, then **switches**. 【指 4 cells】 The step-back has **no network counterpart**: a waiting packet sits in a buffer, but **a waiting robot blocks the way**.
zh: 方法二是**门口规则**。一格宽的门就是**半双工链路**：**一次只走一个方向**。【指上面三格图，从左到右】门先服务一边，对面的车**退出门口 4 格**，把出口让出来；这一边走空了，门就收尾，然后**换向**。【指 4 cells】退让这一条**网络里没有**：等着的数据包待在缓存里，但**等着的车会挡路**。

title: Scheduling 2: queue scheduling at the door
hints: Door = router port with 2 queues (one per direction, robots within 8 cells)
Which queue, for how long = queue scheduling
9 ticks same direction, 21 ticks to switch
Switch every robot 43%; batch of 10: 88%
Tried: limit 80 steps → kept: exhaustive service (serve until empty)
Blocked robots → lowest planner priority
Polling theory assumes arrivals independent: not true here → tested

segs.en: Underneath, the door is a **router port with two queues**, one for each direction: the robots within 8 cells that want to cross. Which queue to serve, and for how long? That is **queue scheduling**.
segs.zh: 往下看，门就是一个**有两个队列的路由器端口**，每个方向一个队列：门两侧 8 格内要过门的车。先服务哪个队列、服务多久？这就是**队列调度**。

segs.en: 【指公式】 Switching is expensive: in the same direction a robot follows every **9 ticks**, but changing direction takes **21**. 【指 43%】 **Round-robin**, one robot per turn, keeps the door busy only **9 out of 21: 43 percent**. 【指 88%】 Ten per turn: **90 out of 102: 88 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指公式】换向很贵：同方向每 **9 拍**跟过一台，换方向要 **21 拍**。【指 43%】**轮转**，每次只放一台，门只有 **9 ÷ 21 = 43%** 的时间在过车。【指 88%】每次放 10 台：**90 ÷ 102 = 88%**。

segs.en: 【指右边第三条】 So we use **polling**. We first capped each turn at 80 steps, then switched to **exhaustive service**: serve a queue **until it is empty**. Polling theory says this is best when switching is expensive.
segs.zh: 【指右边第三条】所以我们用**轮询**。先试过每轮最多 80 步，后来改成**穷尽服务**：一个队列**服务到走空**再换。轮询理论说，换向代价大时这样最好。

segs.en: 【指右边第四条】 Robots stopped by the rule drop to the **lowest priority** in the planner, so they never hold up other robots.
segs.zh: 【指右边第四条】被规则拦住的车在规划里降到**最低优先级**，不会耽误别的车。

segs.en: 【指底部】 One difference: that theory assumes arrivals do not depend on the scheduler. Here arrivals depend on our quota, so the theory is only a guide, and we tested it.
segs.zh: 【指底部】有一点不同：轮询理论假设车什么时候到，和调度规则无关；这里车什么时候到取决于我们的名额，所以理论只能当参考，要靠实验检验。

That is **queue scheduling**. 【指公式】 Switching is expensive: in the same direction a robot follows every **9 ticks**, but changing direction takes **21**. 【指 43%】 **Round-robin**, one robot per turn, keeps the door busy only **9 out of 21: 43 percent**. 【指 88%】 Ten per turn: **90 out of 102: 88 percent**. 【指右边第三条】 So we use **polling**. We first capped each turn at 80 steps, then switched to **exhaustive service**: serve a queue **until it is empty**. Here arrivals depend on our quota, so the theory is only a guide, and we tested it.

title: Scheduling 3: a bug fix in the executor
figs: 图 12 执行器修复示意
hints: Stuck at 22 per 500 ticks
Credit flow control: report a freed slot at once
Executor kept robot in old cell's queue
3 lines → back to 26
en: Third, a **bug fix**. Door 6 was **stuck at 22** robots per 500 ticks. In **credit flow control**, a freed slot must be reported **at once**. 【指上排】 But the official executor **kept a robot in a cell's queue after it left**, so the next robot waited a whole round. 【指下排和 22 → 26】 **Three lines** fixed it: back to **26**.
zh: 第三，**修一个程序错误**。门 6 **卡在每 500 拍 22 台**。**信用流控**要求空位一腾出来就**立刻**报告。【指上排】但官方执行器**在车离开后，那一格的排队名单里还留着它**，后面的车白等一整轮。【指下排和 22 → 26】改了 **3 行**，回到 **26 台**。

segs.en: Third, a **bug fix**. Door 6 was **stuck at 22** robots per 500 ticks. In **credit flow control**, a freed slot must be reported **at once**.
segs.zh: 第三，**修一个程序错误**。门 6 **卡在每 500 拍 22 台**。**信用流控**要求空位一腾出来就**立刻**报告。

segs.en: 【指上排】 But the official executor **kept a robot in a cell's queue after it left**, so the next robot waited a whole round.
segs.zh: 【指上排】但官方执行器**在车离开后，那一格的排队名单里还留着它**，后面的车白等一整轮。

segs.en: 【指下排和 22 → 26】 **Three lines** fixed it: back to **26**.

title: Does it only work on this map? Random doors
figs: 换图测试图（8 张随机门房间图 × 2 种车数）
hints: Worry: tuned on the fixed official map only
Wrote a random door generator → 8 new room maps
199 / 249 robots, 640 runs: wins every map, +86.9%
New problem 1: narrow spots → global cap 138 (Little's law); without it −16.9% on one map
New problem 2: rare deadlock 1,114 → 700 → watchdog 300 ticks, relax rule
Watchdog: no measurable effect on these 8; earlier confirmation +2.30% on 15 generated room-map instances
Hand over to Speaker 4

segs.en: These three changes were all made on the **official map**, where the doors never move. We worried they only work on **this map and these doors**. So we wrote a program that **places doors at random**, and built **8 new room maps**.
segs.zh: 这三项优化都是在官方这张门位置固定的地图上做的。我们担心它们只对**这张图、这些门**有用，所以写了一个**随机生成门位置**的程序，造了 **8 张新的房间图**。

segs.en: 【指左图第一栏】 On each map we ran **199 and 249 robots**, **640 runs** in all. Against the same base, our method **won on every map**, by **86.9 percent** on average.
segs.zh: 【指左图第一栏】每张图跑 **199 台和 249 台**两种车数，一共 **640 局**。和同一底座比，我们的方法**每张图都赢**，平均多 **86.9%**。

segs.en: But the new maps also showed **two problems** that the official map does not have, so we added **two safety nets**.
segs.zh: 但新图也暴露了官方图上没有的**两个问题**，于是我们又加了**两个兜底**。

segs.en: 【指左下卡片】 First, some maps have **narrow spots that our door rules do not cover**. A **global cap** from Little's law limits how many robots hold orders at once. On the official map: **1.76 times 69.2 divided by 500, times 2.23, times 255, is 138 robots**. 【指左图第二栏】 Without the cap, one new map loses **16.9 percent** with 249 robots.
segs.zh: 【指左下卡片】第一，有些图上有**门口规则管不到的窄处**。按 Little 定律加一个**全图上限**，限制同时接单的车数。在官方图上：**1.76 × 69.2 ÷ 500 × 2.23 × 255 = 138 台**。【指左图第二栏】拿掉这个上限，一张新图在 249 台时少了 **16.9%**。

segs.en: 【指右下卡片】 Second, **rare deadlocks**: in one test run, two doors one step apart locked each other, and completions fell from **1,114 to 700**. A **watchdog** from lossless networks fixes this: if a robot waits **300 ticks** and its door has had no entry for 300 ticks, it may skip the door rule for one tick. Networks drop packets here; **we cannot drop robots, so we relax the rule instead**.
segs.zh: 【指右下卡片】第二，**少见的死锁**：有一局里两道只隔一步的门互相锁住，完成数从 **1114 单掉到 700 单**。我们借无损网络的**看门狗**：车等满 **300 拍**、它的门也 300 拍没车进，就允许它这一拍不守门口规则。网络在这时丢包，**我们不能丢车，所以改成放宽规则**。

segs.en: 【指左图第三栏】 Deadlocks are rare, so on these 8 maps the watchdog shows **no measurable effect**. In an earlier confirmation on **15 generated room-map instances**, it added **2.30 percent**. So we keep both safety nets.
segs.zh: 【指左图第三栏】死锁很少见，所以在这 8 张图上看门狗**测不出作用**；在更早一次、**15 个生成房间图实例**上的确认实验里，它多了 **2.30%**。所以两个兜底都留着。

segs.en: Speaker 4 will show the results.
segs.zh: 下面讲者 4 讲结果。

en: These three changes were all made on the **official map**, where the doors never move. We worried they only work on **this map and these doors**. So we wrote a program that **places doors at random**, and built **8 new room maps**. 【指左图第一栏】 On each map we ran **199 and 249 robots**, **640 runs** in all. Against the same base, our method **won on every map**, by **86.9 percent** on average. But the new maps also showed **two problems** that the official map does not have, so we added **two safety nets**. 【指左下卡片】 First, some maps have **narrow spots that our door rules do not cover**. A **global cap** from Little's law limits how many robots hold orders at once. On the official map: **1.76 times 69.2 divided by 500, times 2.23, times 255, is 138 robots**. 【指左图第二栏】 Without the cap, one new map loses **16.9 percent** with 249 robots. 【指右下卡片】 Second, **rare deadlocks**: in one test run, two doors one step apart locked each other, and completions fell from **1,114 to 700**. A **watchdog** from lossless networks fixes this: if a robot waits **300 ticks** and its door has had no entry for 300 ticks, it may skip the door rule for one tick. Networks drop packets here; **we cannot drop robots, so we relax the rule instead**. 【指左图第三栏】 Deadlocks are rare, so on these 8 maps the watchdog shows **no measurable effect**. In an earlier confirmation on **15 generated room-map instances**, it added **2.30 percent**. So we keep both safety nets. Speaker 4 will show the results.
zh: 这三项优化都是在官方这张门位置固定的地图上做的。我们担心它们只对**这张图、这些门**有用，所以写了一个**随机生成门位置**的程序，造了 **8 张新的房间图**。【指左图第一栏】每张图跑 **199 台和 249 台**两种车数，一共 **640 局**。和同一底座比，我们的方法**每张图都赢**，平均多 **86.9%**。但新图也暴露了官方图上没有的**两个问题**，于是我们又加了**两个兜底**。【指左下卡片】第一，有些图上有**门口规则管不到的窄处**。按 Little 定律加一个**全图上限**，限制同时接单的车数。在官方图上：**1.76 × 69.2 ÷ 500 × 2.23 × 255 = 138 台**。【指左图第二栏】拿掉这个上限，一张新图在 249 台时少了 **16.9%**。【指右下卡片】第二，**少见的死锁**：有一局里两道只隔一步的门互相锁住，完成数从 **1114 单掉到 700 单**。我们借无损网络的**看门狗**：车等满 **300 拍**、它的门也 300 拍没车进，就允许它这一拍不守门口规则。网络在这时丢包，**我们不能丢车，所以改成放宽规则**。【指左图第三栏】死锁很少见，所以在这 8 张图上看门狗**测不出作用**；在更早一次、**15 个生成房间图实例**上的确认实验里，它多了 **2.30%**。所以两个兜底都留着。下面讲者 4 讲结果。

title: Results on the official room map
figs: 图 14 逐级结果柱状图
hints: 3 fleet sizes × 20 runs
Bars: starter → champion → fixed executor → ours
+140.5% vs starter
+76.5% vs same base (fairest)
en: Thank you. Results on the **official room map**: three fleet sizes, **20 runs** each. 【指柱状图，从灰到橙】 Each bar adds one step: starter program, champion's assignment, fixed executor, and, in orange, our control. 【指 +140.5%】 Against the starter program: **plus 140.5 percent**. 【指 +76.5%】 The **fairest comparison**, same assignment and same fixed executor, so only our control differs: **plus 76.5 percent**. 【指 618 → 1,106】 With 250 robots: **618 orders become 1,106**.
zh: 谢谢。这是**官方房间图**上的结果：三种车数，每种 **20 局**。【指柱状图，从灰到橙】每根柱子加一步：起始程序、冠军派单、修好执行器，橙色是加上我们的控制。【指 +140.5%】比起始程序：**多 140.5%**。【指 +76.5%】**最公平的比较**是同样派单、同样修好执行器，只差我们的控制：**多 76.5%**。【指 618 → 1,106】250 台车时：**从 618 单到 1106 单**。

segs.en: Thank you. Results on the **official room map**: three fleet sizes, **20 runs** each.
segs.zh: 谢谢。这是**官方房间图**上的结果：三种车数，每种 **20 局**。

segs.en: 【指柱状图，从灰到橙】 Each bar adds one step: starter program, champion's assignment, fixed executor, and, in orange, our control.
segs.zh: 【指柱状图，从灰到橙】每根柱子加一步：起始程序、冠军派单、修好执行器，橙色是加上我们的控制。

segs.en: 【指 +140.5%】 Against the starter program: **plus 140.5 percent**. 【指 +76.5%】 The **fairest comparison**, same assignment and same fixed executor, so only our control differs: **plus 76.5 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指 +140.5%】比起始程序：**多 140.5%**。【指 +76.5%】**最公平的比较**是同样派单、同样修好执行器，只差我们的控制：**多 76.5%**。

segs.en: 【指 618 → 1,106】 With 250 robots: **618 orders become 1,106**.

title: Which parts matter?
figs: 图 16 逐项拿掉与加上
hints: 600 runs, remove one part
Door rule −25.6, quota −13.6, executor −6.7
Door rule alone +29.7, quota alone +29.3, together +76.4
Quota = how many; door rule = how they pass
en: Which parts matter? 【指左边红条】 In **600 runs**, we removed one part at a time. **No door rule: minus 25.6 percent. No quota: minus 13.6. No executor fix: minus 6.7.** 【指右边蓝条】 Alone, the door rule gives **29.7 percent**, the quota **29.3**; together, **76.4**. 【指黄框】 **The quota decides how many robots come. The door rule decides how they pass.**
zh: 哪些部分起作用？【指左边红条】我们跑了 **600 局**，每次拿掉一项：**拿掉门口规则少 25.6%，名额少 13.6%，执行器修复少 6.7%。**【指右边蓝条】单加门口规则 **+29.7%**，单加名额 **+29.3%**；两个一起 **+76.4%**。【指黄框】**名额管来多少车，门口规则管怎么过。**

segs.en: Which parts matter? 【指左边红条】 In **600 runs**, we removed one part at a time. **No door rule: minus 25.6 percent. No quota: minus 13.6. No executor fix: minus 6.7.**
segs.zh: 哪些部分起作用？【指左边红条】我们跑了 **600 局**，每次拿掉一项：**拿掉门口规则少 25.6%，名额少 13.6%，执行器修复少 6.7%。**

segs.en: 【指右边蓝条】 Alone, the door rule gives **29.7 percent**, the quota **29.3**; together, **76.4**.
【指黄框】 **The quota decides how many robots come. The door rule decides how they pass.**
segs.zh: 【指黄框】**名额管来多少车，门口规则管怎么过。**

title: Most ideas failed, and why
figs: 图 18 69 项机制的筛选漏斗
hints: 69 mechanisms
38 measure-first / 23 development / 7 new maps / 1 passed
Every rerouting method lost
Lessons: assumptions break; door 6 sets throughput; confirm on new maps
en: Most of our ideas failed. 【指漏斗从上到下】 We tried **69 network mechanisms**. **38** were dropped after a quick check, **23** failed testing, **7** failed on new maps. **Only one passed: the watchdog.** **Every rerouting idea lost.** 【指三张卡】 Three lessons. **Network assumptions often break for robots.** **Door 6 sets the limit.** **Always confirm on new maps.**
zh: 我们的大多数想法都失败了。【指漏斗从上到下】我们试了 **69 种网络机制**。**38 种**先量一下就放弃，**23 种**没过测试，**7 种**在新图上没确认。**只有看门狗 1 种通过。** **所有换路办法都变差。**【指三张卡】三点教训：**网络的前提在车上常常不成立；上限由门 6 决定；提升一定要换新图确认。**

segs.en: Most of our ideas failed. 【指漏斗从上到下】 We tried **69 network mechanisms**.
segs.zh: 我们的大多数想法都失败了。【指漏斗从上到下】我们试了 **69 种网络机制**。

segs.en: **38** were dropped after a quick check, **23** failed testing, **7** failed on new maps. **Only one passed: the watchdog.** **Every rerouting idea lost.**
segs.zh: **38 种**先量一下就放弃，**23 种**没过测试，**7 种**在新图上没确认。**只有看门狗 1 种通过。** **所有换路办法都变差。**

segs.en: 【指三张卡】 Three lessons. **Network assumptions often break for robots.** **Door 6 sets the limit.** **Always confirm on new maps.**
segs.zh: 【指三张卡】三点教训：**网络的前提在车上常常不成立；上限由门 6 决定；提升一定要换新图确认。**

title: Conclusion
hints: Not smarter robots: count + which side
Hypothesis half right: routing no, scheduling yes
Real warehouse: quota per direction + one direction at a time
Simulation only; re-measure for new layouts
Thank you, questions
en: To finish. 【指 1】 **We did not make each robot smarter.** We controlled **how many robots head for a door, and which side goes first.** 【指 2】 Our guess was **half right**: **routing did not help, scheduling did.** 【指 3】 For a real warehouse: **a quota per direction when giving out orders, and one direction at a time in narrow aisles.** 【指 4】 Limits: this is **simulation only**, and the numbers must be **re-measured for a new layout**. Thank you. Questions are welcome.
zh: 总结一下。【指 1】**我们没有让每台车更聪明**，而是管住**多少车奔向一道门、哪边先走**。【指 2】我们的猜想**对了一半**：**路由没用，调度有效。**【指 3】放到真实仓库：**派单时每个方向一个名额，窄巷一次只放一个方向。**【指 4】局限：**只做了仿真**，换布局要**重新测参数**。谢谢大家，欢迎提问。

segs.en: To finish. 【指 1】 **We did not make each robot smarter.** We controlled **how many robots head for a door, and which side goes first.**
segs.zh: 总结一下。【指 1】**我们没有让每台车更聪明**，而是管住**多少车奔向一道门、哪边先走**。

segs.en: 【指 2】 Our guess was **half right**: **routing did not help, scheduling did.**
segs.zh: 【指 2】我们的猜想**对了一半**：**路由没用，调度有效。**

segs.en: 【指 3】 For a real warehouse: **a quota per direction when giving out orders, and one direction at a time in narrow aisles.**
segs.zh: 【指 3】放到真实仓库：**派单时每个方向一个名额，窄巷一次只放一个方向。**

segs.en: 【指 4】 Limits: this is **simulation only**, and the numbers must be **re-measured for a new layout**.
segs.zh: 【指 4】局限：**只做了仿真**，换布局要**重新测参数**。

segs.en: Thank you. Questions are welcome.
segs.zh: 谢谢大家，欢迎提问。
